q: What are the emissions of an electric cargo bike for deliveries?
title: Electric cargo bike delivery emissions
short: Only the charging electricity counts in use, at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. A cargo bike uses a few kWh a day, so a day's deliveries come to a few kg CO2, far below a diesel van. Building the battery and bike is Scope 3 Category 2.

ol: Charging kWh from a meter or charger log.

p: If you own the bikes and pay for charging, it is your Scope 2. If a courier does the delivery, it sits in your Scope 3 transport.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.

sources.label: CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector
